title: facility egress security overlay
question: Can occupants leave safely during an emergency while unauthorized entry to restricted assets remains controlled and observable?
scenario: Regional operations room: A utility is relocating a control-support team to a shared office building.
focalRelation: Site selection and perimeter shape exposure; deterrence, delay, detection, visitor management, restricted zones, response, safety, and fail-safe behavior must coexist; emergency egress cannot be treated as ordinary ingress.

nodes.label: Public Entrance
nodes.detail: Visitors and staff enter the shared building through the public approach.

nodes.label: Reception Boundary
nodes.detail: Reception identifies visitors, confirms sponsors, issues bounded credentials, and directs circulation.

nodes.label: Restricted Operations Room
nodes.detail: The control-support room contains assets and work that require an explicitly restricted physical zone.

nodes.label: Approved Personnel
nodes.detail: Named personnel enter only for an authorized purpose and remain subject to escort or access conditions.

nodes.label: Emergency Egress
nodes.detail: The exit path permits safe evacuation during alarm or power loss without granting uncontrolled reentry.

nodes.label: People Safety
nodes.detail: Life-safety design keeps occupants and responders able to leave or enter as required during an emergency.

edges.label: must remain compatible with the applicable design

lanes.label: Public and personnel side
lanes.rule: Visitors and approved personnel approach from outside the restricted room.

lanes.label: Entry and egress controls
lanes.rule: Reception, governed entry, and emergency egress apply distinct ingress and life-safety rules.

lanes.label: Restricted operations and life safety
lanes.rule: The operations room remains restricted while occupants retain safe emergency exit.

prediction.prompt: Can occupants leave safely during an emergency while unauthorized entry to restricted assets remains controlled and observable?

options.label: Fail-lock every ingress and egress door, then rely on responders to override locks during an emergency.
options.feedback: Life-safety egress requirements can override a security preference and require independent safe operation.

options.label: Preserve the restricted boundary during power loss, even when occupants cannot use the designated exit.
options.feedback: Life-safety egress can require fail-safe exit behavior while ingress, alarm, and reentry remain controlled.

options.label: Design separate safe egress and controlled ingress behaviors, with response and monitoring that preserve life safety.
options.feedback: More barriers can delay occupants or responders and create unsafe failure behavior without improving protection.

prediction.hint: Security zoning must coexist with code-compliant life-safety egress.

retry.prompt: A proposed operations site has inexpensive space but sits in a floodplain with one utility feed and no practical alternate work location. What should the design review conclude?

options.label: Choose the site because perimeter barriers can compensate for environmental and utility exposure
options.feedback: Barriers address some entry threats; they do not remove flood, utility, continuity, and safe-operations dependencies.

options.label: Reassess site selection, environmental exposure, utility resilience, safety, and alternate operations together
options.feedback: Correct. Facility security begins with site and dependency choices, not only doors and guards.

options.label: Accept the site if the server room is placed inside a restricted area
options.feedback: A restricted room does not resolve site-wide flood, utility, evacuation, or continuity risk.

retry.hint: Choose the design that preserves safe evacuation while alarming and recording the boundary crossing.

takeaway: Use the case evidence to apply this relation: Site selection and perimeter shape exposure; deterrence, delay, detection, visitor management, restricted zones, response, safety, and fail-safe behavior must coexist; emergency egress cannot be treated as ordinary ingress.
assumptions: Only entities and claims anchored in the canonical unit or explicitly labeled hypothetical scenario are used.
A highlighted path means the learner is inspecting that path; it does not assert the event occurred.
The current source is authoritative for facts; this treatment reorganizes presentation without changing canonical content.
The lesson teaches one bounded decision and does not claim to exhaust every jurisdiction, vendor implementation, architecture, attack, or exception.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: The boundary states preserve public approach, visitor circulation, restricted entry, emergency egress, reentry control, and life-safety priority. They use named zones and relations rather than a spatial floor-plan overlay.

learningJob.plainExplanation: Occupants must be able to exit safely during an emergency while unauthorized entry and re-entry remain controlled and observable. The exact behavior depends on applicable life-safety requirements.
learningJob.visualReasoningGain: A plan view would materially add route, direction, door behavior, and boundary reasoning; the current abstract row map adds little beyond prose.

spatialPlan.title: Controlled entry and safe egress use separate directional paths
spatialPlan.description: A visitor enters through reception and an authorization gate. During an emergency, occupants exit directly to safety; the alarm and exterior control prevent that life-safety path from becoming uncontrolled re-entry.
notes: The emergency path is available from the inside without requiring normal entry authorization.
Opening the emergency exit raises an alarm; it does not authorize entry from outside.
A blocked or locked egress route is a life-safety failure even when the restricted boundary remains intact.
